chunks: Among what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) that has been established regarding the salat (prayer)? He said:

“Eight rakʿahs at zawāl, two rakʿahs after al-ẓuhr, two rakʿahs before al-ʿaṣr, two rakʿahs after al-maghrib, thirteen rakʿahs in the latter part of the night, including al-watr, and the two rakʿahs of al-fajr.”
I said: So is this all that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has established? He said: Yes.

Then Abū al-Khaṭṭāb said: What do you think if he is strong enough and adds more? He said: So he sat up, and he had been reclining, and said: “If you have strength, then perform it as it used to be performed; and just as it is not in any hour of the day, neither is it in any hour of the night. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
‘And during parts of the night, then glorify [Him].’

It is therefore possible that he permitted Zurārah to limit himself to these prayers because of an excuse that Zurārah had, due to the abundance of his occupations, the neglect of which would bring harm upon him, or because of some reason among the reasons that would justify that for him; otherwise it would not have been permissible. If the matter is as such, then it is permissible for him to restrict himself to them, because in our view, whenever a person has an excuse such that his occupation with the nawāfil would harm him with respect to it, it is permissible for him to leave them altogether, since they are not among those things for whose omission punishment is deserved. We shall present later what indicates that, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills; and that which clarifies what we have mentioned, namely that the excuse was in Zurārah.

key_terms.آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ: the parts or hours of the night
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic tradition in regard to worship
key_terms.الْعُذْرَ: a valid excuse that justifies omission or restriction
key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: the witr prayer within the night prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the sunnah rakʿahs of the daily prayers according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the established sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding the recommended daily salat (prayer), including daytime, night, and dawn nawāfil. It also indicates that limiting oneself to some of these prayers may be allowed in the presence of a valid excuse, and cites a Quranic phrase concerning glorification during parts of the night.
